segments.name: s1
segments.text: Before a network service ships, someone should find out exactly where it breaks.

segments.name: s2
segments.text: AETHER-NIM is a crash-test lab for fiber networks. It starts healthy: seventeen nodes, twenty links, five demand pairs, held together by one number, algebraic connectivity: five point three seven.

segments.name: s3
segments.text: Now the gap. Dashboards show that something broke. Meetings decide what to do next. Hours pass. But the answer is already inside the graph.

segments.name: s4
segments.text: So we break it, for real. A bridge link fails. Lambda two collapses to exactly zero. Two islands form. Throughput craters. Measured, not imagined.

segments.name: s5
segments.text: Diagnosis runs two sources at once. A structured incident report goes to NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory. And at the exact same moment, the twin calls the Tavily Search API for live fiber-outage context from the real web.

segments.name: s6
segments.text: Nemotron returns root causes, a ranked repair plan, risks and confidence, as strict JSON. And you can see the live citations on screen.

segments.name: s7
segments.text: Now the rule. AI proposes. The engine disposes. Every proposed action is validated against the live graph, planned by a deterministic optimizer, with rollback armed.

segments.name: s8
segments.text: The repair executes. A separate verifier recomputes every metric from scratch: success. One component. Five out of five demand pairs. Throughput restored. In seconds, not hours.

segments.name: s9
segments.text: Every claim on this screen was measured, repaired and proven. AETHER-NIM. Trust, but verify, as software. Live demo and code below.
